questions.enonce_markdown:
Draw a large and neatly labelled diagram of the general plan of human blood circulation.

**OR**

Describe the general plan of human blood circulation. *(8 marks)*
questions.corrige_markdown:
**Drawing required (no figure supplied):** draw the heart in the middle, with the **lungs** on one side and the **body organs** (head, liver, intestine, kidneys, legs) below, and label the following.

- The **heart**, with the **right atrium, right ventricle, left atrium and left ventricle**.
- **Pulmonary circulation**: the **pulmonary artery** carries deoxygenated blood from the right ventricle to the **lungs**, and the **pulmonary veins** return oxygenated blood to the left atrium.
- **Systemic circulation**: the **aorta** leaves the left ventricle and gives the **carotid artery** (to the head), the **hepatic artery** (liver), the **mesenteric artery** (intestine), the **renal arteries** (kidneys) and the **iliac arteries** (legs); deoxygenated blood returns by the **superior vena cava** (from the head and arms) and the **inferior vena cava** (from the rest of the body), which carry it to the right atrium; the **renal veins** and the **hepatic vein** also join the inferior vena cava.
- The **hepatic portal vein**, which carries blood from the intestine to the liver.
- Capillary networks in the lungs and in the organs, with arrows showing the direction of flow.

**Description (alternative):** in humans there is a **double circulation**: the blood passes **twice** through the heart in one complete circuit. In the **pulmonary circulation**, the right ventricle pumps deoxygenated blood through the pulmonary artery to the lungs, where it takes up oxygen and loses carbon dioxide, and the pulmonary veins return it to the left atrium. In the **systemic circulation**, the left ventricle pumps oxygenated blood through the aorta and its branches to all the organs of the body, where it gives up oxygen and picks up carbon dioxide, and the venae cavae return the deoxygenated blood to the right atrium. The blood is kept at high pressure for the second circuit because it goes back through the heart.

questions.enonce_markdown: Explain how a molecule of glucose absorbed in the ileum will be transported to the brain. *(6 marks)*
questions.corrige_markdown:
1. Glucose is **absorbed** (by diffusion and active transport) through the wall of a **villus** of the ileum into the **blood capillaries**.
2. The capillaries join to form the **hepatic portal vein**, which carries the blood rich in glucose to the **liver**.
3. In the liver some glucose is converted to glycogen for storage, and the rest passes on in the blood into the **hepatic vein**.
4. The hepatic vein joins the **inferior vena cava**, which brings the blood to the **right atrium** of the heart, then to the **right ventricle**.
5. The right ventricle pumps the blood through the **pulmonary artery** to the **lungs**, and the **pulmonary vein** brings it back to the **left atrium**, then to the **left ventricle**.
6. The left ventricle pumps the blood into the **aorta**, from which it goes into the **carotid artery** to the **brain**.
7. In the capillaries of the brain, glucose **diffuses** from the blood into the brain cells, where it is used in respiration.

questions.enonce_markdown: In tabular form state SIX differences between veins and arteries. *(6 marks)*
questions.corrige_markdown:
| Arteries | Veins |
|---|---|
| Carry blood **away from** the heart | Carry blood **towards** the heart |
| Have **thick, muscular and elastic** walls | Have **thin** walls with less muscle and elastic tissue |
| Have a **narrow** lumen | Have a **wide** lumen |
| Have **no valves** (except at the base of the aorta and pulmonary artery) | Have **valves** to prevent the backflow of blood |
| Blood flows at **high pressure**, in pulses | Blood flows at **low pressure**, smoothly |
| Carry **oxygenated** blood (except the pulmonary artery) | Carry **deoxygenated** blood (except the pulmonary veins) |
| Usually deep inside the body | Often near the surface of the body |
